copy.bis: Ang mga kuko hinimo sa patay nga selula sa panit nga puno sa keratin. Ginapanalipdan nila ang dulo sa tudlo ug motubo og mga 3 milimetro matag buwan.

How big is the Napoleon wrasse?

The Napoleon wrasse can grow up to 2 meters long and is known for the big hump on its forehead — it's one of the largest reef fish and is endangered worldwide.
copy.tl:
Gaano kalaki ang Napoleon wrasse?

Ang Napoleon wrasse ay maaaring lumaki ng hanggang 2 metro at kilala sa malaking utong sa noo nito — isa ito sa pinakamalaking isda sa bahura at endangered na sa buong mundo.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadako ang Napoleon wrasse?

Ang Napoleon wrasse makaabot og 2 metro ang gitas-on ug nailhan sa dakong bukog sa agtang niini — usa kini sa pinakadako nga isda sa bahura ug globally endangered na.

copy.tl: Ang bacterial cellulose na nasa nata de coco ay pinag-aaralan din bilang materyal para sa benda ng sugat — malinis, basa, at malakas na hibla na tumutulong sa paggaling ng balat.
copy.bis: Ang bacterial cellulose nga anaa sa nata de coco gitun-an usab isip materyal sa benda sa samad — limpyo, basa, ug kusgan nga hilo nga makatabang sa pag-ayo sa panit.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify the products of traditional biotechnology through fermentation (e.g. cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco)

copy.en:
Why is sugar added when making nata?

Bacteria need sugar as food and energy to build cellulose — that's why sugar is added to coconut water, so more nata forms, faster.
copy.tl:
Bakit nilalagyan ng asukal ang paggawa ng nata?

Kailangan ng bakterya ng asukal bilang pagkain at lakas para makagawa ng cellulose — kaya dinaragdagan ng asukal ang tubig-niyog para mas marami at mas mabilis mabuo ang nata.
copy.bis:
Nganong dugangan ug asukal ang paghimo sa nata?

Nanginahanglan ang bakterya ug asukal isip pagkaon ug kusog aron makahimo og cellulose — mao nga dugangan ug asukal ang tubig-lubi aron mas daghan ug mas paspas maporma ang nata.

copy.bis: Ang National Greening Program motabang sa pagpakunhod sa deforestation pinaagi sa paghatag sa mga mag-uuma og economically important nga mga tanom sama sa cacao, falcate, ug mga kahoy nga namunga.

copy.tl: Protektado ng batas ng Pilipinas ang mga katutubong ligaw na baboy, kaya bawal ang basta-bastang pangangaso sa kanila.
copy.bis: Gipanalipdan sa balaod sa Pilipinas ang lumad nga ihalas nga baboy, mao nga gidili ang basta-basta nga pagpangayam kanila.

copy.bis: Ang laki nga baboy ihalas adunay hait nga bangkil nga mogawas sa ilang baba, gamiton sa pagpakig-away sa ubang baboy ug pagpanalipod sa kaugalingon.

copy.en: A natural dye is a color taken from plants, animals, or minerals instead of factory chemicals, used to color cloth, paper, or food!
copy.tl: Ang natural dye ay kulay na galing sa halaman, hayop, o mineral imbes na gawa sa pabrika, ginagamit para kulayan ang tela, papel, o pagkain!
copy.bis: Ang natural dye usa ka kolor gikan sa tanom, mananap, o mineral imbes nga gikan sa pabrika, gigamit aron koloran ang panapton, papel, o pagkaon!

copy.tl: Bago ang synthetic dyes, gumamit ang mga tao ng natural dyes mula sa halaman tulad ng indigo para sa blue-purple na kulay at annatto seeds para sa orange-yellow!
copy.bis: Sa wala pay synthetic dyes, naggamit ang mga tawo og natural dyes gikan sa tanom sama sa indigo para sa blue-purple nga kolor ug annatto seeds para sa orange-yellow!

copy.tl: Ang makapal at mabuhok na balat ng niyog ay tinatawag na bunot o coir! Ginagawa itong lubid, basahan sa pinto, at panghugas ng sahig na marami sa Pilipinas.
copy.bis: Ang baga ug buhokon nga panit sa lubi gitawag og bunot o coir! Himuong pisi, basahan sa pultahan, ug panghugas sa salog nga daghan sa Pilipinas.

copy.en:
How do indigenous weavers in the Philippines make beautiful cloth?

They make cloth from natural fiber by hand using a loom! They twist, dye, and weave beautiful cultural patterns, like the T'nalak cloth of the T'boli people.
copy.tl:
Paano gumagawa ng magagandang tela ang mga katutubong manghahabi sa Pilipinas?

Gumagawa sila ng tela mula sa natural fiber gamit ang habihan! Pinipilipit, kinukulay, at hinahabi nila ang magagandang disenyo, tulad ng T'nalak ng mga T'boli.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo og nindot nga panapton sa mga lumad nga maghahabol sa Pilipinas?

Naghimo sila ug panapton gikan sa natural fiber gamit ang habolan! Pilipiton, koloran, ug habolon nila ang nindot nga disenyo, sama sa T'nalak sa mga T'boli.

Did you know we can make fine cloth from pineapple leaves?

Yes, it’s called Pina! Thin fibers are pulled from pineapple leaves, washed, and woven into fine cloth. It is famous in Aklan for making barong Tagalog.
copy.tl:
Alam mo bang pwedeng gumawa ng magandang tela mula sa dahon ng pinya?

Oo, tinatawag itong Pina! Hinihila ang manipis na fibers mula sa dahon ng pinya, hinuhugasan, at hinahabi para maging magandang tela. Sikat ito sa Aklan sa paggawa ng barong Tagalog.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga pwede tang magbuhat ug nindot nga panapton gikan sa dahon sa pinya?

Oo, gitawag kini nga Pina! Bunloton ang nipis nga fibers gikan sa dahon sa pinya, hugasan, ug habolon aron mahimong nindot nga panapton. Bantogan kini sa Aklan sa paghimo ug barong Tagalog.

copy.en:
Why do some clothes say 'hand wash' only?

Some natural fibers need careful washing! Wool shrinks in hot water, and silk tears easily. That's why they must be washed gently!
copy.tl:
Bakit may mga damit na nakasabing 'hand wash' lang?

Kailangan maingat hugasan ang ilang natural fiber! Umuurong ang wool sa mainit na tubig, at madaling masira ang silk. Kaya banayad lang ang paghuhugas!
copy.bis:
Nganong naay sinina nga giingon nga 'hand wash' lang?

Kinahanglan amping labhan ang mga natural fiber! Momubo ang wool sa init nga tubig, ug dali maguba ang silk. Mao nga hinay lang ang paghugas!

Where do natural materials come from?

They come straight from nature—like plants, animals, or the ground! Think wood, cotton, wool, rock, and sand.
copy.tl:
Saan nagmumula ang mga natural na materyales?

Galing sila direkta sa kalikasan—tulad ng halaman, hayop, o lupa! Isipin mo ang kahoy, bulak, wool, bato, at buhangin.
copy.bis:
Asa nagagikan ang natural nga materyales?

Gikan sila direkta sa kinaiyahan—sama sa mga tanom, hayop, o yuta! Hunahunaa ang kahoy, gapas, wool, bato, ug balas.

Never taste an unknown chemical! Use an indicator instead to find out if it is an acid or base.

Pwede bang tikman ang kemikal para malaman kung asido o base?

Huwag tikman ang hindi kilalang kemikal! Gumamit ng indicator imbes para malaman kung asido o base ito.

Pwede ba tilawi ang kemikal aron mahibaw-an kung asido o base?

Ayaw tilawi ang wala mailhi nga kemikal! Gamita ang indicator imbes aron mahibaw-an kung asido o base kini.

Which element has the highest atomic number in the periodic table?

Oganesson! With an atomic number of 118, it holds the highest atomic number in the periodic table.
copy.tl:
Anong elemento ang may pinakamataas na atomic number sa periodic table?

Oganesson! Na may atomic number na 118, ito ang elementong may pinakamataas na atomic number sa periodic table.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga elemento ang may pinakataas nga atomic number sa periodic table?

Oganesson! Nga adunay atomic number nga 118, mao kini ang elemento nga may pinakataas nga atomic number sa periodic table.

Newton's first law is also called the law of inertia!

Ang unang batas ni Newton ay tinatawag ding batas ng inersya (law of inertia)!

Unsay laing ngalan sa unang balaod sa paglihok ni Newton?

Ang unang balaod ni Newton gitawag usab nga law of inertia (balaod sa inersya)!

copy.en: Isaac Newton created the three laws of motion to describe how objects move when forces push or pull them!
copy.tl: Gumawa si Isaac Newton ng tatlong batas ng galaw na naglalarawan kung paano gumagalaw ang mga bagay kapag may tumutulak o humihila!
copy.bis: Naghimo si Isaac Newton sa tulo ka balaod sa paglihok nga nagsaysay kung giunsa paglihok sa mga butang kung adunay magtukmod o magbira!

copy.en:
How did Newton prove white light has all rainbow colors?

He used a prism! It showed that white light is actually made of all rainbow colors.
copy.tl:
Paano ipinakita ni Newton na may lahat ng kulay ang puting liwanag?

Gumamit siya ng prisma! Ipinakita nito na ang puting liwanag ay binubuo ng lahat ng kulay ng bahaghari.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpakita ni Newton nga ang puti nga kahayag naay tanang kolor?

Nagamit niya ang prisma! Gipakita niini nga ang puti nga kahayag gilangkuban sa tanang kolor sa bangaw.

copy.en: Newton's first law is also called the law of inertia because it perfectly explains the inertia of objects!
copy.tl: Tinatawag ding batas ng inersya ang unang batas ni Newton dahil ipinapaliwanag nito ang inersya ng mga bagay!
copy.bis: Ang unang balaod ni Newton gitawag usab nga balaod sa inertia tungod kay gipasabot niini ang inertia sa mga butang!

Does nickel silver have real silver?

Nope! It's an alloy of copper, zinc, and nickel that just looks like silver. It's used for cutlery and decorations!
copy.tl:
May tunay ba pilak ang nickel silver?

Wala! Ito ay alloy ng tanso, zinc, at nickel na mukhang pilak lang. Ginagamit ito sa kubyertos at dekorasyon!
copy.bis:
Naay tinuod ba nga pilak ang nickel silver?

Wala! Kini usa ka alloy sa tanso, zinc, ug nickel nga morag pilak. Gigamit kini sa kubyertos ug dekorasyon!

copy.en: Night is cooler because no sunlight is heating our side of Earth, so the ground slowly loses its warmth!
copy.tl: Mas malamig sa gabi dahil walang sikat ng Araw na nagpapainit sa ating bahagi ng Mundo, kaya unti-unti itong lumalamig!
copy.bis: Mas bugnaw sa gabii kay walay sidlak sa Adlaw nga nag-init sa atong bahin sa Kalibotan, mao nga hinay-hinay kining mibugnaw!

Why does Mayon's summit glow at night?

When Mayon is erupting, people see a night glow on the summit! It's a repeating sign that hot lava is near the crater.
copy.tl:
Bakit nag-iilaw ang tuktok ng Mayon sa gabi?

Kapag sumasabog ang Mayon, nakikita ng tao ang night glow sa tuktok! Ito ay repeating sign na mainit na lava ang nasa crater.
copy.bis:
Nganong nagdan-ag ang tumoy sa Mayon sa gabii?

Kung mo-alsa ang Mayon, makita sa mga tawo ang night glow sa tumoy! Timailhan kini nga init nga lava naa sa crater.

assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about the Sun's role in providing light and warmth, but it does not involve making suggestions, group/class discussion, or confirming/recording ideas from secondary sources as required by the competency.

Why do we use lamps at night?

Because sunlight is gone! It is a daily reminder that outdoor seeing and warming come from the Sun.
copy.tl:
Bakit gumagamit tayo ng ilaw sa gabi?

Dahil wala na ang sikat ng araw! Ito ay paalala na ang liwanag at init sa labas ay galing sa Araw.
copy.bis:
Nganong mogamit ta og suga sa gabii?

Kay wala na ang adlaw! Kini pahimangno nga ang kahayag ug kainit sa gawas gikan sa Sun.

Which river is the longest, and which carries the most water?

The Nile is usually the longest, but the Amazon carries more water than any other river in the world!
copy.tl:
Aling ilog ang pinakamahaba, at alin ang nagdadala ng pinakamaraming tubig?

Ang Ilog Nile ang itinuturing na pinakamahaba, pero ang Ilog Amazon ang nagdadala ng pinakamaraming tubig sa lahat ng ilog!
copy.bis:
Asang suba ang labing taas, ug asang nagdala og pinakadaghang tubig?

Ang Suba sa Nile giila nga labing taas, apan ang Suba sa Amazon nagdala og pinakadaghang tubig sa tanang suba!

How does a bahay kubo stay cool in tropical heat?

It's built from nipa, bamboo, and other natural materials that insulate and allow air flow, keeping the interior cool!

Paano nananatiling malamig ang bahay kubo sa init ng tropiko?

Gawa ito sa nipa, kawayan, at iba pang natural na materyales na nagsisilbing insulator at nagpapahintulot ng air flow para panatilihing malamig ang loob!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpabilin nga malamig ang bahay kubo sa tropical nga init?

Gitukod kini gikan sa nipa, kawayan, ug uban pang natural nga materyales nga nag-insulate ug naghatag og air flow aron mapabilin nga malamig ang sulod!

What is the most common gas in the air we breathe?

Nitrogen! It makes up about 78% of the air around us.

Nitrogen! Bumubuo ito ng halos 78% ng hangin sa paligid natin.

Unsa ang labing daghan nga gas sa hangin nga atong ginhanglan?

Nitrogen! Mga 78% niini sa hangin sa palibot nato.

copy.tl: Ang nitrogen ay isang nakatagong gas! Ito ay walang kulay at walang amoy, kaya hindi mo ito makikita o maaamoy.
copy.bis: Ang nitrogen usa ka nagtago nga gas! Kini walay kolor ug walay baho, mao nga dili nimo kini makita o mabaho.

Hindi magagamit ng halaman ang nitrogen gas mula sa hangin — may espesyal na bakterya na nagbabago nito para masipsip ng ugat.

Ngano nga dili magamit sa tanom ang nitrogen sa hangin?

Dili magamit sa tanom ang nitrogen gas gikan sa hangin — adunay espesyal nga bakterya nga nag-usab niini aron masuyop sa gamot.

copy.bis: Puno sa nitrogen ang hangin, apan dili kini direktang magamit sa tanom — hangtod himoon kining abono sa bakterya sa gamot sa legume.

Kaya bang gamitin ng halaman ang nitrogen gas sa hangin?

Hindi direktang magagamit ng halaman ang nitrogen gas sa hangin — kailangan muna itong mabago sa ibang anyo.

Makagamit ba ang tanom og nitrogen gas sa hangin direkta?

Dili direkta magamit sa tanom ang nitrogen gas sa hangin — kinahanglan una kini usbon ngadto sa laing porma.

copy.bis: Grabe ka bugnaw sa likidong nitrogen sa -196 degrees Celsius! Agad niini makapayelo ang bisan unsang mahikap, mao kining gigamit sa labs para sa biological sample ug medical procedures.

copy.bis: Ang nitroheno importanteng bahin sa protina ug DNA, ang mga molekula nga naghimo ug nagpadagan sa buhing selula.

copy.bis: Ang kawanangan halos vacuum — halos walay hangin nga maginhawa! Mao nga ang mga astronaut magsul-ob og espesyal nga suit ug tangke sa oksiheno. Dili madungog ang tingog kay nagkinahanglan og hangin aron molahos!

It only states that these methods were used, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: people kept food from spoiling by drying, salting, and smoking it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about minimizing harmful changes in materials (e.g., restricting burning, handling reactive materials). The card is about food preservation before refrigerators, which is unrelated to minimizing harmful material changes. No direct or prerequisite support.

copy.en: Long before refrigerators existed, people kept food from spoiling by drying, salting, and smoking it!
copy.tl: Noong wala pang refrigerator, ginagamit ng mga tao ang pagpapatuyo, pag-aasin, at pagtatapa para tumagal ang pagkain!
copy.bis: Sa wala pa ang repridyireytor, gigamit sa mga tawo ang pagpauga, pag-asin, ug pagpaaso aron molungtad ang ilang pagkaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We cannot see color without light!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe sources of light and their use in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that light is needed to see color, but it does not describe sources of light or their uses in everyday situations, which is the focus of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We cannot see color without light!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not involve guided science activities, nor does it explore sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, or its uses. It only states a basic fact about light and color perception.

copy.en:
Why is it hard to see colors in a dark place?

We cannot see color without light! Without it, colors are just hard to see.
copy.tl:
Bakit mahirap makita ang mga kulay sa madilim na lugar?

Hindi natin makikita ang kulay kapag walang liwanag! Kaya sa madilim na lugar ay mahirap makita ang mga kulay.
copy.bis:
Ngano lisod makita ang mga kolor sa ngitngit nga dapit?

Dili nato makita ang kolor kung walay kahayag! Busa sa ngitngit nga dapit lisod kaayo makita ang mga kolor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: No machine is perfectly efficient!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses machines in general and energy loss as heat from friction, but does not address simple machines (inclined planes, wedges, levers, pulleys) or their advantages/limitations through guided investigation. It shares vocabulary about machines but does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because some energy is always lost as heat, often from friction.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that friction causes energy loss as heat, which is background knowledge for the idea that friction can produce heat. However, it does not demonstrate how friction produces heat or investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction, so it does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en:
Why can't any machine be 100% efficient?

Because some energy is always lost as heat, often from friction. No machine is perfectly efficient!
copy.tl:
Bakit walang makinang 100% efficient?

Dahil laging may bahagi ng enerhiyang nasasayang bilang init, kadalasan dahil sa friction. Walang makinang perpektong efficient!
copy.bis:
Ngano walay makina nga 100% efficient?

Tungod kay kanunay adunay bahin sa enerhiya nga mausik isip kainit, kasagaran tungod sa friction. Walay makina nga perpektong efficient!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each snowflake gets its own shape because it passes through slightly different cold and moisture as it falls
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions moisture and cold, which are part of the water cycle, but it does not explain the role of the water cycle in the environment. It only explains why snowflakes have unique shapes, not how water cycles through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, etc.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each snowflake gets its own shape because it passes through slightly different cold and moisture as it falls
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on weather-related factors (cold and moisture) but does not involve observing, recording, or describing weather changes or patterns in a local area. It is about snowflake shape variation, not weather observation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each snowflake gets its own shape because it passes through slightly different cold and moisture as it falls
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: Snowflakes are solid water, but the card does not describe changes in state (solid to liquid to gas) or how temperature causes phase changes. It only mentions cold and moisture affecting shape, not state transitions.

copy.en:
Why does every snowflake have a unique shape?

Each snowflake gets its own shape because it passes through slightly different cold and moisture as it falls, creating a huge variety of patterns!
copy.tl:
Bakit may kakaibang hugis ang bawat snowflake?

Nakakakuha ng kakaibang hugis ang bawat snowflake dahil dumadaan ito sa bahagyang magkaibang lamig at halumigmig habang bumabagsak, kaya napakaraming pattern ang lumalabas!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga lainlain ang porma sa matag snowflake?

Makakuha og kaugalingong porma ang matag snowflake tungod kay moagi kini sa gamay nga lahi nga kabugnaw ug kaumog samtang nahulog, mao nga daghan kaayo nga pattern ang motungha!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they are stable, non-reactive gases with eight valence electrons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes noble gases as non-reactive, which touches on chemical reactivity, but the competency G4-M-3 focuses on describing chemical properties of materials such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. The card does not describe these properties or provide examples of materials that burn, react, or degrade; it only states that noble gases are non-reactive. This is a peripheral mention of reactivity rather than direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Group 18 elements are called noble gases, and they are stable, non-reactive gases with eight valence electrons, except helium which has only two.
copy.tl: Ang mga elemento sa Group 18 ay tinatawag na noble gases, at sila ay stable, non-reactive na mga gas na may walong valence electrons, maliban sa helium na may dalawa lang.
copy.bis: Ang mga elemento sa Group 18 gitawag ug noble gases, ug sila kay stable, dili reaktibo nga mga gas nga adunay walo ka valence electrons, gawas sa helium nga adunay duha lang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound travels farther and faster underwater than in air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sound transfer underwater and its effect on marine animals, but the competency focuses on exploring and describing how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations (e.g., ringing bell, hearing noises). The card does not address everyday sound sources or the process of sound production/transfer in common contexts, so it only shares the broad topic of sound transfer.

copy.en: Sound travels farther and faster underwater than in air, so noise from big ships can disturb whales and dolphins that depend on sound to talk and find food!
copy.tl: Mas malayo at mas mabilis maglakbay ang tunog sa ilalim ng tubig kaysa sa hangin, kaya ang ingay ng malalaking barko ay nakakaabala sa mga balyena at dolphin na umaasa sa tunog para mag-usap at maghanap ng pagkain!
copy.bis: Mas layo ug mas paspas mobiyahe ang tingog ilalom sa tubig kay sa hangin, busa ang kasaba sa dagkong barko makasamok sa mga balyena ug dolphin nga nagsalig sa tingog aron makig-istorya ug mangita og pagkaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fossil fuels are coal, oil, and natural gas. They are non-renewable because they don't form again quickly once we use them up!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines fossil fuels and explains non-renewability. It does not address generation of electricity in the Philippines, impacts on human activities or the environment, or evaluation using secondary sources, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fossil fuels are coal, oil, and natural gas. They are non-renewable because they don't form again quickly once we use them up!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fossil fuels but does not discuss chemical reactions such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, or respiration, nor their impacts on natural and built environments. It is only topically related.

copy.en:
What are fossil fuels and why are they non-renewable?

Fossil fuels are coal, oil, and natural gas. They are non-renewable because they don't form again quickly once we use them up!
copy.tl:
Ano ang fossil fuels at bakit sila non-renewable?

Ang fossil fuels ay ang coal, oil, at natural gas. Sila ay non-renewable dahil hindi sila agad nabubuo ulit kapag naubos na natin!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang fossil fuels ug nganong non-renewable man sila?

Ang fossil fuels mao ang coal, oil, ug natural gas. Gitawag silang non-renewable kay dili dali nga maporma pag-usab kung mahurot na nato!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Nonrenewable energy runs out and cannot be quickly replaced.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines nonrenewable energy and gives examples, which is background knowledge for evaluating renewable/non-renewable electricity generation in the Philippines, but it does not address generation, the Philippines, or impacts on human activities and the environment.

copy.en: Nonrenewable energy runs out and cannot be quickly replaced. Examples are coal, oil, and natural gas.
copy.tl: Ang nonrenewable energy ay mauubos at hindi mabilis mapapalitan. Ang mga halimbawa ay karbon, langis, at natural gas.
copy.bis: Ang nonrenewable energy mahurot ug dili dali mapulihan. Ang mga pananglitan mao ang karbon, lana, ug natural gas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A blood pressure reading around 120/80 mmHg is considered normal for most adults
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: A normal-number reading is not describing homeostasis as balance among all body systems.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A blood pressure reading around 120/80 mmHg is considered normal for most adults
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: A 120/80 reading is trivia, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en: A blood pressure reading around 120/80 mmHg is considered normal for most adults.
copy.tl: Ang presyon ng dugo na malapit sa 120/80 mmHg ay itinuturing na normal para sa karamihan ng mga adulto.
copy.bis: Ang presyon sa dugo nga duol sa 120/80 mmHg giisip nga normal para sa kadaghanan sa mga hamtong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The North Equatorial Current flows westward across the Pacific Ocean, reaching the eastern coast of the Philippines before it splits!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an ocean current and the eastern coast of the Philippines, which are bodies of water and a coastline, but it does not identify local examples of landforms/bodies of water nor describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment. It only states the current's direction and destination.

copy.en: The North Equatorial Current flows westward across the Pacific Ocean, reaching the eastern coast of the Philippines before it splits!
copy.tl: Ang North Equatorial Current ay dumadaloy pakanluran sa Pacific, umaabot sa silangang baybayin ng Pilipinas bago ito humati!
copy.bis: Ang North Equatorial Current nagaagos pakasadpan sa Pacific, moabot sa sidlakang baybayon sa Pilipinas una kini mabahin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The name of the North Star is Polaris, the star in the direction of north!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the name of the North Star and that it points north. It does not explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons, which is the core of G6-E-9.

copy.en:
Do you know the special name of our North Star?

The name of the North Star is Polaris, the star in the direction of north!
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba ang espesyal na pangalan ng North Star natin?

Ang pangalan ng North Star ay Polaris, ang bituin na nasa direksyon ng hilaga!
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo ang espesyal nga ngalan sa atong North Star?

Ang ngalan sa North Star kay Polaris, ang bituon nga anaa sa direksyon sa amihanan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the real name of the North Star is Polaris
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the name of a star (Polaris). The competency requires guided activities to observe and describe celestial objects, including stars. Naming a star does not directly support the observation/description skill or the guided activity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the real name of the North Star is Polaris
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks to explain why ancient cultures relied on constellations for direction and seasons. The card merely identifies Polaris as the North Star; it does not discuss constellations, navigation, seasons, or ancient cultural practices.

copy.en:
What is the real name of the North Star?

When you look up at the night sky, the real name of the North Star is Polaris!
copy.tl:
Ano ang tunay na pangalan ng North Star?

Kapag tumingin ka sa langit sa gabi, ang tunay na pangalan ng North Star ay Polaris!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang tinuod nga ngalan sa North Star?

Kung motan-aw ka sa langit sa gabii, ang tinuod nga ngalan sa North Star mao ang Polaris!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: sailors have used it as a direction guide for centuries
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions direction guidance by sailors, but the competency specifically asks about ancient human cultures relying on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons. The card does not discuss ancient cultures, constellations, or seasonal verification; it only explains Polaris as a fixed direction marker.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It appears not to move while other stars circle around it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Polaris appearing stationary while other stars move, which relates to observing star motion, but it does not involve guided activities to explore and record how and when celestial objects can be seen moving across the sky. It is a factual explanation, not an activity-based exploration or recording task.

copy.en:
Why is Polaris called the North Star?

Polaris is almost directly above Earth's north pole! It appears not to move while other stars circle around it, and sailors have used it as a direction guide for centuries.
copy.tl:
Bakit tinatawag na North Star ang Polaris?

Ang Polaris ay halos direktang nasa itaas ng north pole ng Earth! Tila hindi ito gumagalaw habang ang ibang bituin ay lumilibot sa paligid, at ginamit ito ng mga mandaragat bilang gabay sa direksyon.
copy.bis:
Nganong gitawag nga North Star ang Polaris?

Ang Polaris halos direkta sa ibabaw sa north pole sa Yuta! Daw dili kini nagalihok samtang ang ubang mga bituin naglibot sa palibot, ug gigamit sa mga manlalayag isip giya sa direksyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lean forward a little and pinch the soft part of your nose.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives first-aid instructions for a nosebleed. It does not identify the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how they work, which is the required competency. The mention of the nose is incidental and unrelated to respiratory system function.

copy.en:
What should you do for a nosebleed?

Lean forward a little and pinch the soft part of your nose.
copy.tl:
Ano ang gagawin kapag dumudugo ang ilong?

Yumuko nang bahagya at pisilin ang malambot na bahagi ng ilong.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang buhaton kon magdugo ang ilong?

Yukbo gamay ug pislita ang humok nga bahin sa ilong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: one shake alone isn't a volcano pattern
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
assignedReviews.reason: The card makes a general point that earthquakes do not always lead to eruptions and that a single event does not establish a pattern. It does not discuss patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years, nor does it involve assessing predictability or discussion with family/community members as required by the competency.

copy.en: The Philippines has many earthquakes that never cause an eruption, so one shake alone isn't a volcano pattern!
copy.tl: Maraming lindol sa Pilipinas ang hindi nagdudulot ng pagputok, kaya isang pagyanig lang ay hindi volcano pattern!
copy.bis: Daghan kaayog linog sa Pilipinas nga walay pagputok, mao nga usa ra ka pag-uyog dili volcano pattern!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun matters as a light source and as an energy source
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make suggestions about the importance of the Sun to living things for a group or class discussion and confirm and record ideas by referring to trustworthy secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that the Sun is important as a light and energy source, which touches on the content of the Sun's importance to living things. However, the competency requires students to make suggestions for a group/class discussion and to confirm/record ideas by referring to trustworthy secondary sources. The card provides no discussion activity, no suggestions, and no reference to secondary sources, so it does not directly support the skill or action of the competency.

copy.en:
Is the Sun just there to make us warm, or is there more to it?

The Sun matters as a light source and as an energy source, so it does so much more than just warm us!
copy.tl:
Ang Araw ba ay nandiyan lang para magpainit sa atin, o may iba pa siyang ginagawa?

Ang Araw ay mahalaga bilang pinagmumulan ng ilaw at enerhiya, kaya hindi lang siya basta nagpapainit sa atin!
copy.bis:
Ang Sun ba anaa ra para magpainit kanato, o naa pa'y lain?

Ang Sun importante ingon nga source sa suga ug enerhiya, mao nga dili lang siya basta nagpainit kanato!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Past eruptions show what a volcano can do, but they don't make the next blast perfectly predictable like a ticking clock!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
assignedReviews.reason: The card makes a general statement about volcanic eruption predictability, but does not discuss patterns of eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years, nor involve family/community discussion as required by the competency. It shares the topic of eruption predictability but provides no direct instructional support for the specific pattern-analysis skill.

copy.en:
Can we predict the exact time a volcano will erupt?

Past eruptions show what a volcano can do, but they don't make the next blast perfectly predictable like a ticking clock!
copy.tl:
Kaya ba nating hulaan ang eksaktong oras ng pagputok ng bulkan?

Ang mga nakaraang pagputok ay nagpapakita ng kayang gawin ng bulkan, pero hindi nito ginagawang eksaktong oras ang susunod na pagsabog tulad ng relo!
copy.bis:
Kaya ba natong matagna ang eksaktong oras sa pagputok sa bulkan?

Ang mga miaging pagputok makatabang masabtan unsa ang mahimo sa bulkan, pero dili kini makapahimo nga eksakto ang oras sa sunod nga pagsabog sama sa orasan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rainfall warning can happen even without a high wind signal!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only distinguishes rainfall warnings from wind signals; it does not describe the weather conditions associated with a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by PAGASA. The competency requires describing those conditions, which the card does not address.

copy.en: A rainfall warning can happen even without a high wind signal! They are two related but different alerts for wind-signal weather and rain-warning weather.
copy.tl: Maaaring magkaroon ng rainfall warning kahit walang mataas na wind signal! Dalawa itong magkaugnay pero magkaibang alerto para sa hangin at ulan.
copy.bis: Pwede naay rainfall warning bisan walay taas nga wind signal! Duha kini nga magkaugnay pero lahi nga alerto para sa hangin ug ulan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Nuclear energy comes from the nucleus of atoms when they are split or joined together!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the nucleus but does not describe the structure of an atom (nucleus and electron shells) or support drawing it. It only states a fact about nuclear energy, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Nuclear energy comes from the nucleus of atoms when they are split or joined together!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the source of nuclear energy, not about evaluating renewable/non-renewable electricity generation in the Philippines or its impacts on human activities and the environment. No connection to the competency's subject.

copy.en:
Where does nuclear energy come from?

Nuclear energy comes from the nucleus of atoms when they are split or joined together!
copy.tl:
Saan nagmumula ang nuclear energy?

Ang nuclear energy ay nagmumula sa nukleus ng mga atom kapag ito ay nahahati o nagsasama!
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang nuclear energy?

Ang nuclear energy gikan sa nucleus sa mga atomo kung kini bahinon o iusa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it’s still non-renewable because mined uranium can run out
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that nuclear energy is non-renewable because uranium can run out, but it does not evaluate how renewable/non-renewable electricity generation impacts human activities and the environment, nor does it reference the Philippines or secondary sources. This is only a related fact about non-renewable energy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Nuclear energy comes from splitting uranium atoms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses nuclear energy and uranium, not the structure of an atom in terms of nucleus and electron shells. It does not support drawing or describing atomic structure.

copy.en: Nuclear energy comes from splitting uranium atoms! It’s not a fossil fuel, but it’s still non-renewable because mined uranium can run out.
copy.tl: Ang nuclear energy ay galing sa paghati ng uranium atoms! Hindi ito fossil fuel, pero non-renewable pa rin dahil ang minahin na uranium ay maaaring maubos.
copy.bis: Ang nuclear energy gikan sa pagbahin sa uranium atoms! Dili kini fossil fuel, apan non-renewable gihapon kay ang uranium gimina ug mahimong mahurot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nucleus is the atom's center, and it is made up of protons and neutrons!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that the nucleus contains protons and neutrons. This is background knowledge needed before the differentiation competency can be taught.

copy.en:
What is inside the nucleus of an atom?

The nucleus is the atom's center, and it is made up of protons and neutrons!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nasa loob ng nucleus ng isang atom?

Ang nucleus ang sentro ng atom, at ito ay binubuo ng mga proton at neutron!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naa sa sulod sa nucleus sa usa ka atom?

Ang nucleus mao ang sentro sa atom, ug kini gilangkuban sa mga proton ug neutron!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nucleus is the cell's control center — it holds the DNA and directs everything the cell does.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use proper techniques in observing and identifying the parts of a cell with a microscope such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about the nucleus as a cell part, but does not address the competency's focus on proper microscope techniques for observing and identifying cell parts. It provides no instruction on using a microscope or identifying multiple cell structures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nucleus is the cell's control center — it holds the DNA and directs everything the cell does.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions DNA being held in the nucleus, but does not explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits. It lacks any discussion of genes, chromosomes, inheritance, or how traits are passed on.

copy.en:
What is the control center of a cell?

The nucleus is the cell's control center — it holds the DNA and directs everything the cell does.
copy.tl:
Ano ang control center ng selula?

Ang nukleyus ang siyang control center ng selula — dito nakatago ang DNA at ito ang namamahala sa mga gawain nito.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang control center sa selula?

Ang nukleyus mao ang control center sa selula — dinhi anaa ang DNA ug nagdumala kini sa mga buluhaton sa selula.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They are found right in the center of the atom, in a place called the nucleus!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that protons and neutrons are located in the nucleus. It does not mention electron shells, nor does it involve drawing the atom's structure. This is useful background for drawing the nucleus but does not directly teach the drawing skill or the electron-shell component.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They are found right in the center of the atom, in a place called the nucleus!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives the location of protons and neutrons (in the nucleus) but does not differentiate subatomic particles by symbol, mass, charge, or location of electrons. It only partially addresses the 'location' aspect for two of the three particles, so it is background rather than direct instruction for the full competency.

copy.en:
Where do protons and neutrons hang out inside an atom?

They are found right in the center of the atom, in a place called the nucleus!
copy.tl:
Saan nagtatambay ang protons at neutrons sa loob ng atomo?

Matatagpuan sila sa gitna ng atomo, sa isang lugar na tinatawag na nucleus!
copy.bis:
Asa nagpuyo ang protons ug neutrons sulod sa atomo?

Makita sila sa sentro sa atomo, sa usa ka lugar nga gitawag og nucleus!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
